headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[launches tree plantation drive]] in Barishal
headline: PM Tarique Rahman launches tree plantation drive in Barishal
summary: The Prime Minister urged citizens to nurture saplings to ensure survival, stating that planting alone is not enough.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inaugurated a tree plantation programme in Gournadi upazila of Barishal, planting coconut and neem saplings along the banks of the newly re-excavated Sarikal-Batajor Canal.
During the event, the Prime Minister emphasized that planting trees is only the beginning and stressed the need for proper care to ensure the saplings survive.
He compared the care of young saplings to the care of children, urging everyone to look after them daily.
Approximately 2,500 saplings were planted during the drive, which was formally inaugurated under the slogan 'Bangladesh First'.
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon also participated in the the programme by planting a saplings.
Following the plantation drive, the Prime Minister distributed Family Cards to women heads of beneficiary families in Batajor.
Thousands of BNP leaders and supporters lined the 34-kilometre road from Gournadi to Barishal city to welcome the Prime Minister.
The Prime Minister's itinerary includes another tree plantation programme along the Sagardi Canal in Barishal city and an organisational meeting of the BNP.
caption:
Planting is not the end of the job. PM Tarique Rahman urges citizens to nurture saplings like children to ensure survival.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inaugurated a tree plantation programme in Gournadi upazila of Barishal, planting coconut and neem saplings along the banks of the newly re-excavated Sarikal-Batajor Canal.

During the event, the Prime Minister emphasized that planting trees is only the beginning and stressed the need for proper care to ensure the saplings survive.

He compared the care of young saplings to the care of children, urging everyone to look after them daily.

Approximately 2,500 saplings were planted during the drive, which was formally inaugurated under the slogan 'Bangladesh First'.

Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon also participated in the the programme by planting a saplings.

Following the plantation drive, the Prime Minister distributed Family Cards to women heads of beneficiary families in Batajor.

Thousands of BNP leaders and supporters lined the 34-kilometre road from Gournadi to Barishal city to welcome the Prime Minister.

The Prime Minister's itinerary includes another tree plantation programme along the Sagardi Canal in Barishal city and an organisational meeting of the BNP.

headline_marked: Govt raises [[cash incentive to 5% for RMG exporters]] using local yarn
headline: Govt raises cash incentive to 5% for RMG exporters using local yarn
summary: The move aims to revive the struggling textile spinning industry and reduce reliance on imported raw materials.
details: The government has increased the cash incentive for export-oriented garment manufacturers using locally produced yarn or fabric from 1.5 percent to 5 percent.
According to a Bangladesh Bank circular, this enhanced incentive applies to export shipments made between July 1, 2026, and June 30, 2027.
To qualify, exporters must provide documentary proof that they sourced their yarn or fabric from domestic producers.
The decision follows repeated requests from textile mill owners, who argued that previous incentive cuts had made imported yarn cheaper than local alternatives.
Until January 2024, the incentive stood at 4 percent, but was later reduced to 1.5 percent as Bangladesh prepared for LDC graduation.
Industry leaders noted that lower incentives led to a surge in imports, particularly from India, hurting the local cotton industry.
A BTMA director highlighted that local mills face pressure from rising gas and electricity prices, higher wages, and competition from supported Indian mills.
caption:

To qualify, exporters must provide documentary proof that they sourced their yarn or fabric from domestic producers.

The decision follows repeated requests from textile mill owners, who argued that previous incentive cuts had made imported yarn cheaper than local alternatives.

Until January 2024, the incentive stood at 4 percent, but was later reduced to 1.5 percent as Bangladesh prepared for LDC graduation.
